The fastest way to understand that path is to watch one query fail, repair it, and then change the rules around it.

children: The runtime identity does not own tables. The owner does not log in. Ownership carries authority beyond an ACL entry: an owner can alter or drop the object and grant its privileges, and a table owner normally bypasses row security. Migration automation deliberately becomes the owner while running DDL, so ownership and default privileges remain stable when login credentials rotate.
